title: Using commonMZ rules with CAMERA
text: MZ_CAMERA() accepts three modes: "pos" positive-ion LC-MS, "neg" negative-ion LC-MS, "ei" electron-ionisation GC-MS. warn_clash argument flags pairs rules whose mass differences fall within given ppm tolerance distinguished mass alone. Browse full table — sort column use search box filter name mass difference:
code: rules_pos <- MZ_CAMERA(mode = "pos", warn_clash = TRUE, clash_ppm = 5) # A tibble: 2 × 2   first       second   <chr>       <chr> 1 [M+H-NH3]+  [M+NH4]+ 2 [M+H-C3H4]+ [M+H+(CH3)2CO-H2O]+ (acetone cond.) Example:  rules=rules[            !grepl("[M+NH4]+",rules[,"name"],fixed=TRUE)         ,] rules_pos %>% mutate(massdiff = round(massdiff, 4)) rules_neg <- MZ_CAMERA(mode = "neg", warn_clash = TRUE, clash_ppm = 5) # A tibble: 2 × 2   first        second   <chr>        <chr> 1 [M-H-HCOOH]- [M-H+HCOOH]- 2 [M-H-C3H4]-  [M-H+(CH3)2CO-H2O]- (acetone cond.) title: Using commonMZ rules with CAMERA
text: example uses mm14, xcmsSet bundled CAMERA package (134 peaks, single sample, positive mode). data, replace mm14 xcmsSet xcms peak detection. Step 1 — create xsAnnotate object: Step 2 — group co-eluting peaks retention time window (FWHM-based): multi-sample data cross-sample correlation step refines groups : Step 3 — annotate isotope peaks: Step 4 — annotate adducts fragments commonMZ rules. CAMERA requires plain data.frame, tibble, wrap .data.frame(): multiplier controls highest oligomer CAMERA consider (e.g. [2M+H]+, [3M+H]+). ppm mzabs set matching tolerance; CAMERA applies whichever window wider, high-resolution data keep mzabs small (0.005–0.01) rely ppm.
code: library(CAMERA)  data("mm14") xsa <- xsAnnotate(mm14, polarity = "positive") xsaF <- groupFWHM(xsa, perfwhm = 0.6, intval = "into") xsaF <- groupCorr(xsaF, cor_eic_th = 0.7, pval = 1e-6,                   calcIso = FALSE, calcCiS = FALSE, calcCaS = TRUE) xsaI <- findIsotopes(xsaF, ppm = 10, mzabs = 0.01, intval = "into") cam_result <- findAdducts(xsaI,                           ppm        = 10,                           mzabs      = 0.01,                           multiplier = 3,                           polarity   = "positive",                           rules      = as.data.frame(rules_pos_clean))

Second, height difference sulfur signal: 34S towers every carbon/nitrogen/oxygen combination also reach +2 — fine-structure version 40-fold excess already spotted coarse pattern, now specific competing hypothesis (¹³C¹³C) specific, different mass.
code: plot_level <- function(pattern, level, title) {   base <- pattern %>% filter(label == "") %>% pull(mz)   d <- pattern %>%     mutate(nominal = round(mz - base)) %>%     filter(nominal == level) %>%     mutate(element = sub(",.*", "", label),            element = sub("^[0-9]+", "", element),            col = ifelse(label == "" | grepl(",", label), "combo", element),            col = ifelse(col %in% names(COL), col, "combo"))   ggplot(d, aes(mz, abundance, colour = col)) +     geom_segment(aes(xend = mz, y = 0, yend = abundance),                  linewidth = 2.2, lineend = "round") +     geom_text(data = slice_max(d, abundance, n = min(6, nrow(d))),               aes(label = label),               angle = 90, hjust = -0.15, size = 3.1, colour = "grey20") +     scale_colour_manual(values = COL, guide = "none") +     scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.0001)) +     scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .35))) +     labs(x = "m/z (Da)", y = "% of M (monoisotopic)", title = title) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +     theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) } plot_level(pat, 1, paste(formula, "M+1")) plot_level(pat, 2, paste(formula, "M+2"))

what: Step 3: would your instrument resolve the candidates?
title: Isotope fine structure
text: every pair isotopologues nominal level, table reports Orbitrap resolving power (quoted m/z 200) two Gaussian peaks show ~50% valley , enough centroid algorithm find two separate peaks. Two peaks equal height separated 1.5 × FWHM produce valley; translating R@200 Orbitrap convention scales 1/sqrt(m/z): Every pair M+2 candidates 0.01% abundance. R@200 Orbitrap resolving power two peaks show ~50% valley. closest pair (13C, 33S vs 18O, 0.0015 Da apart) needs R ~ 131,003 @200 resolve two peaks.
code: R_at_mz <- function(mz, R_ref, mz_ref = 200) R_ref * sqrt(mz_ref / mz)  separations <- function(pattern, level, mz_ref = 200, min_abundance = 0.01) {   base <- pattern %>% filter(label == "") %>% pull(mz)   d <- pattern %>%     mutate(nominal = round(mz - base)) %>%     filter(nominal == level, abundance >= min_abundance) %>%     mutate(label = ifelse(label == "", "M", label))   if (nrow(d) < 2) return(tibble())   ix <- combn(seq_len(nrow(d)), 2)   map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(ix)), function(i) {     ra <- d[ix[1, i], ]; rb <- d[ix[2, i], ]     sep_da   <- abs(ra$mz - rb$mz)     m_avg    <- (ra$mz + rb$mz) / 2     Rreq     <- 1.5 * m_avg / sep_da     Rref_req <- Rreq / sqrt(mz_ref / m_avg)     tibble(a = ra$label, b = rb$label,            abundance_a_pct = round(ra$abundance, 3),            abundance_b_pct = round(rb$abundance, 3),            separation_Da = round(sep_da, 5),            R_at_mz = round(Rreq), R_at200 = round(Rref_req))   }) %>% arrange(R_at200) }  ion_mz <- base_mz + 1.007276   # [M+H]+ in positive mode  sep2 <- separations(pat, 2) sep2 %>%   knitr::kable(col.names = c("a", "b", "abundance a %", "abundance b %",                               "separation (Da)", paste0("R at m/z ", round(ion_mz)), "R @200"),                caption = "Every pair of M+2 candidates above 0.01% abundance. R@200 is the Orbitrap resolving power at which the two peaks show a ~50% valley.") best <- sep2 %>% slice_min(separation_Da, n = 1) %>% slice(1) cat(sprintf("The closest pair (`%s` vs `%s`, %.4f Da apart) needs R ~ %s @200 to resolve as two peaks.",             best$a, best$b, best$separation_Da, format(best$R_at200, big.mark = ",")))

title: Isotope fine structure
text: isotope_profile() turns fine-structure table simulated peak shapes resolving power. Pass actual resolving power ion’s m/z ([M+H]⁺ m/z 150), converting instrument’s R @ 200 specification R_at_mz(): 15,000 ³⁴S peak single, slightly lopsided blob; ¹³C¹³C shoulder invisible. 60,000 unmistakable second peak. Fine structure yes/property molecule; question can answer know whether instrument show .
code: Rs <- c(15000, 60000, 120000) R_label <- function(r) sprintf("R = %s @200", format(r, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)) pat2 <- pat %>% mutate(nominal = round(mz - base_mz)) %>% filter(nominal == 2)  prof <- map_dfr(Rs, function(r)   isotope_profile(pat2, resolution = R_at_mz(mean(pat2$mz), r)) %>%     mutate(R = R_label(r)))  p <- ggplot(prof, aes(mz, intensity)) +   geom_area(fill = BLUE, alpha = .25) +   geom_line(colour = BLUE, linewidth = .8) +   geom_rug(data = pat2, aes(x = mz),            inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", colour = "grey30", linewidth = .6) +   facet_wrap(~ factor(R, levels = map_chr(Rs, R_label)), ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.0001)) +   labs(x = "m/z (Da)", y = "simulated intensity (% of M)") +   theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +   theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0)) ggplotly(p, tooltip = c("x", "y"))

what: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
text: Wraps enviPat::isopattern() compute exact fine isotopic structure neutral molecular formula: every isotopologue combination threshold, exact mass abundance relative monoisotopic (base) peak. Unlike nominal-mass isotope pattern (M, M+1, M+2, ...), resolves individual contributors within nominal level – e.g. M+2 satellite sulfur-containing compound really 34S isotopologue (13C, 13C) isotopologue sitting two different exact masses, function tells apart.

title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern
text: formula molecular formula string, e.g. "C5H11NO2S". threshold minimum abundance keep, percent base peak. charge charge state passed enviPat::isopattern(). applies electron-mass correction intrinsically charged species (e.g. metal ion); add proton adduct. simulate ion [M+H]+, leave charge = 0 (default, .e. neutral formula's pattern) add adduct's mass difference mz afterwards, e.g. pattern$mz + 1.007276 protonation – massdiff convention used MZ_CAMERA.

title: Fine isotopologue pattern for a molecular formula — isotope_fine_pattern

code: mz_diff_lookup(   delta,   tol = 100,   unit = c("ppm", "Da"),   ref_mz = NULL,   mode = c("both", "pos", "neg"),   table = mz_diff_table(match.arg(mode)) )

title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
text: delta observed difference, Da. tol tolerance. ppm default (usual way instrument's mass accuracy quoted); switch unit = "Da" flat window instead. ref_mz supplied ppm tolerance applied relative ref_mz (.e. window ref_mz * tol / 1e6), matching scale returned error_ppm column. ref_mz NULL tolerance instead ppm DIFFERENCE, either peak's m/z – small delta unrealistically tight window (10 ppm 1 Da delta 0.00001 Da), since true uncertainty difference comes peaks' mass accuracy, size gap . Widen tol accordingly, supply ref_mz, pass absolute unit = "Da" tolerance already know window want. unit "ppm" (default) "Da". ref_mz reference m/z ppm figures relative , typically parent ion's m/z. Instrument mass accuracy quoted ppm measured m/z, difference two peaks judged m/z peaks measured , size gap: 0.002 Da error 1 Da difference 2000 ppm difference 6.7 ppm 300 Da parent ion, latter realistic number. Supplying ref_mz makes unit = "ppm" tolerance returned error_ppm column relative . default NULL keeps legacy behaviour dividing abs(delta), recommended small deltas. mode passed mz_diff_table table supplied. table table mz_diff_table; computed automatically mode omitted. Pass avoid recomputing calling repeatedly (e.g. every peak pair spectrum).

title: Look up an observed m/z difference against the theoretical differences table — mz_diff_lookup
